scenes.text: An interrupted coding agent should not become another task for the developer. Dovet keeps observable working state so a new authorized agent can continue without making you reconstruct the session. Keep the work. Change the agent.

This managed task has an explicit objective, approved source files, a spending policy, and acceptance checks. Dovet does not claim access to private reasoning, unsaved bytes, or arbitrary Codex Desktop sessions.

The managed Codex worker has made a real change. The operator deliberately interrupts the owned turn. The local service stays running, and another writer remains blocked until termination is confirmed.
Dovet seals selected files into content-addressed artifacts. Credential-like files and build outputs are omitted and listed. A failed capture cannot replace the last verified checkpoint.
This scene remains blocked until the release records a successful Strands decision from Amazon Bedrock. The final narration will describe only the evidence produced by that run.
This scene remains blocked until an authorized replacement worker completes the synthetic importer fixture. No replay or manually written fixture will be presented as a live recovery.
A worker saying done is only a candidate result. Protected checks run independently against an identified snapshot. Missing evidence and changed tests remain failures.
Strands can recommend. Deterministic policy decides. Approvals are bound to one action and snapshot, budgets reject unknown cost, and lease expiry alone never grants a second writer.
The Codex plugin is a short-lived bridge. The independent local daemon owns durable state. The public website and demo use synthetic evidence and keep local-machine control private.
